subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as an additive per-agent config contract, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 be the landing path?
rationale: The source-reproduced gap is real, but adding this config surface changes public configuration, session-state behavior, and provider/model/auth-profile routing, so automation should not create a competing fix or choose the permanent contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor the additive per-agent contract
options.body: Approve the config direction, require deep-merge semantics plus docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR or a narrowed replacement as the landing path.

options.title: Narrow to compaction model first
options.body: Accept only `agents.list[].compaction.model` initially and defer broader compaction/contextPruning knobs to a later design issue.

options.title: Keep defaults-only behavior
options.body: Decline the config expansion and close or redirect the implementation PRs, leaving users with global defaults or separate instances.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the additive per-agent contract
recommendation.body: Approve the config direction, require deep-merge semantics plus docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR or a narrowed replacement as the landing path.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent per-agent defaults and model fallback work makes vincentkoc the strongest available owner for the config-contract decision.
